CLO1.text: Basic approaches to strategy formulation in tech environments.

CLO3.text: Key stages of market planning for tech/software products.

1.topic: Marketing in a Changing World & Core Marketing Concepts (Tech products, platforms, digital services)
lines: Marketing in a Changing World & Core Marketing Concepts (Tech products, platforms, digital services)
Understanding Marketing: Definition, scope, and evolution of marketing in modern technology ecosystems.
Core Concepts: Needs, wants, demands, exchanges, transactions, and relationships.
Value Creation: Delivering customer value through digital solutions and software platforms
Marketing Management Orientations: Production, Product, Selling, Marketing, and Societal Marketing Concepts.
The 4 Ps introduced as the backbone for every later topic

2.topic: Creating Customer Value and Satisfaction in Tech Products & Digital Services
lines: Creating Customer Value and Satisfaction in Tech Products & Digital Services
Traditional vs. digital marketing, current ad-spend/growth data (sets up the digital block)
The 4 principles of digital marketing: attract, engage, convert, sustain

3.topic: Customer Value Framework: Perceived customer value vs. acquisition cost.
lines: Customer Value Framework: Perceived customer value vs. acquisition cost.
Customer Satisfaction & Retention: Metrics for measuring satisfaction, zero-friction UX, and churn rate management.
Customer Equity & Lifetime Value: Calculating Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) and managing long-term customer equity.
Engagement Strategies: Digital touchpoints, user onboarding, and continuous customer relationship building

4.topic: Strategic Planning and the Marketing Process in Technology Companies & IT Startups
lines: Strategic Planning and the Marketing Process in Technology Companies & IT Startups
Strategic Planning Process: Defining corporate mission, setting objectives, and business portfolio design
Portfolio Analysis Models: Boston Consulting Group (BCG) Matrix and GE/McKinsey Matrix
Marketing Strategy & Mix: Formulating the 4 Ps (Product, Price, Place, Promotion) for tech enterprises.
The Marketing Plan: Key sections, executable roadmap design, and budgeting
Structure of a marketing plan (feeds the term project)
Product Levels & Classifications: Core customer value, actual product, augmented product; consumer vs. industrial goods.
Services Marketing: Intangibility, inseparability, variability, perishability (Service-Profit Chain).
Branding Strategy: Brand equity, brand name selection, brand extensions, and co-branding.
Product Line & Mix Decisions: Width, length, depth, and consistency of product offerings.

5.topic: Analyzing the Micro and Macro Marketing Environment in the Tech Industry
lines: Analyzing the Micro and Macro Marketing Environment in the Tech Industry
Microenvironment Analysis: Key actors—suppliers, marketing intermediaries, competitors, publics, and customers
Tech Regulatory & Ethics: Data privacy laws (GDPR, CCPA), intellectual property rights, and compliance for tech products.

6.topic: Marketing Research, Information Systems (MIS), and Introduction to Web Analytics
lines: Marketing Research, Information Systems (MIS), and Introduction to Web Analytics
Marketing Information Systems (MIS): Internal databases, competitive intelligence, and marketing research systems
Marketing Research Process: Defining problems, research design, data collection, and analysis
Quantitative & Qualitative Methods: Surveys, focus groups, A/B testing, and telemetry data collection
First look at Google Analytics (sets up Week 13)
Data Ethics: User consent, data anonymization, and ethical analytics usage.

7.topic: Consumer Markets and Consumer Buyer Behavior (Consumer software, mobile apps, hardware)
lines: Consumer Markets and Consumer Buyer Behavior (Consumer software, mobile apps, hardware)
Influencing Factors: Cultural, social, personal, and psychological drivers of consumer decisions.
Buyer Decision Process: Problem recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, purchase decision, post-purchase behavior.
Technology Adoption Life Cycle: Innovators, early adopters, early majority, late majority, and laggards. Crossing the Chasm preview

8.topic: Business Markets (B2B IT Solutions, Enterprise Software) and Business Buyer Behavior
lines: Business Markets (B2B IT Solutions, Enterprise Software) and Business Buyer Behavior
B2B vs. B2C Dynamics: Characteristics, market structures, and demand types (derived, inelastic, fluctuating).
The Enterprise Buying Center: Roles in procurement (Users, Influencers, Buyers, Deciders, Gatekeepers). RFPs
B2B Buying Process: Problem recognition through vendor performance review in enterprise software/IT.
Institutional & Government Markets: Public sector procurement, RFPs (Request for Proposals), and bidding systems.

9.topic: Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning (STP) for Software & Tech Products
lines: Market Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning (STP) for Software & Tech Products
Market Segmentation: Geographic, demographic, psychographic, behavioral, and technographic bases.
Target Market Selection: Undifferentiated, differentiated, concentrated (niche), and micromarketing.
Differentiation & Value Proposition: Identifying competitive advantages and crafting core value statements.
Positioning Strategy: Perceptual mapping, positioning statements, and brand re-positioning.
Midterm Examination

11.topic: Digital Marketing Deep-Dive I — Channels & Content
lines: Digital Marketing Deep-Dive I — Channels & Content
SEO, content marketing, email, affiliate, influencer marketing
Social media marketing (SMM) fundamentals
Shopify (making website, purchasing domain, adding products)
Assignment: audit a real tech brand's channel mix
New Product Development (NPD) Process: Idea generation, screening, concept testing, marketing strategy, business analysis, development, test marketing, commercialization.
Agile & Lean Approaches: Minimum Viable Product (MVP) development, feedback loops, and rapid iteration.
Product Life-Cycle (PLC) Stages: Introduction, growth, maturity, decline—strategies at each stage.
Crossing the Chasm: Bridging the gap between visionaries (early adopters) and pragmatists (early majority).

12.topic: Digital Marketing Deep-Dive II — Platforms & Setup
lines: Digital Marketing Deep-Dive II — Platforms & Setup
Instagram, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Facebook as marketing tools
Students create a business/company page as a graded task
Prep for the ad-platform lab in Week 12
Distribution Channels & Digital Logistics: App Stores, API Marketplaces, and Cloud Distribution
Marketing Channel Structure: Direct vs. indirect distribution channels; channel levels.
Digital & Cloud Distribution: App stores, API marketplaces, SaaS web portals, and continuous deployment networks.
Channel Management & Conflict: Vertical vs. horizontal marketing systems; multi-channel conflict management.
Supply Chain & Digital Logistics: Order processing, inventory management, CDN distribution, and infrastructure management.

13.topic: Digital Advertising Platform (Google Ads + Meta Ads Manager)
lines: Digital Advertising Platform (Google Ads + Meta Ads Manager)
Campaign structure, audience targeting, budgets, bidding
Each student/team builds a live-style campaign in a sandbox/demo account
This is the required teaching-tool component for placing digital ads

14.topic: Web & Ad Analytics — Measuring the Week-12 Campaign
lines: Web & Ad Analytics — Measuring the Week-12 Campaign
Integrated Marketing Communication (IMC) Strategy: Digital Ads, DevRel (Developer Relations), PR
The Promotion Mix: Integrating advertising, PR, personal selling, sales promotion, and direct marketing.
Communication Process: Sender, encoding, message, media, decoding, receiver, response, feedback, noise.
Steps in Developing Effective IMC: Identifying target audience, determining objectives, designing message, selecting channels, establishing budget.
Tech Community Marketing: Developer Relations (DevRel), open-source advocacy, technical documentation as a conversion tool.
CTR, CPC, CPA, ROAS, conversion tracking
Students pull performance data from their own Week-12 campaign
Google Analytics dashboard walkthrough

15.topic: IMC, DevRel & Free Digital-Marketing Certification Sprint
lines: IMC, DevRel & Free Digital-Marketing Certification Sprint
Integrated marketing communication, growth hacking, DevRel
Direct & Online Marketing: Growth hacking tactics, lifecycle email marketing, search advertising (SEM/SEO), and retargeting.
In-class time to complete one approved free/low-cost certificate (see Materials)
Deliverable: certificate + 1-page reflection linking it to the Week-12 campaign
Lock-in, network effects, defensive moats
Marketing Plan / Term Project presentations
Final Exam
